title: Constant Rate Codes with Fully Addressable Transversal T: Good Codes, Sparse Checks
abstract: Recent work by Wills constructed codes with constant rate and transversal $T$. Extending this line of work, we construct asymptotically good CSS codes with \textbf{fully addressable} transversal $T$, permitting selective control over which logical qubits receive a $T$ gate. We also give Pauli-LDPC codes with transversal $T$ and growing distance at vanishing rate; and a protected-subsystem construction with fully addressable transversal $T$, constant protected rate, distance $Ω(\sqrt n)$, and sparse (non-Pauli) checks. More generally, we obtain asymptotically good binary codes with full transversal addressability for every fixed finite-order one-qubit gate, retaining CSS realizations for dyadic phase gates such as $\sqrt T$ and using generally nonadditive codes for rotations such as $R_z(π/7)$. The remaining challenge is to construct asymptotically good Pauli-LDPC codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford one-qubit gates.
summary: This paper develops advanced theoretical constructions for quantum error-correcting codes, focusing on achieving constant rate while supporting fully addressable transversal gates like the T gate. By combining algebraic geometry and coding theory, the authors establish new bounds on code performance and address the critical challenge of implementing arbitrary logical gates fault-tolerantly.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct quantum error-correcting codes (specifically CSS codes) that possess constant rate, fully addressable transversal gates (like the T gate), and maintain good asymptotic parameters.
main_result: The authors construct asymptotically good CSS codes with fully addressable transversal T gates, and also provide constructions for sparse protected subsystems and Pauli-LDPC codes with transversal T.
method: The work employs advanced techniques from algebraic geometry (e.g., rational functions on curves) and coding theory to enforce specific phase identities required for transversal gate implementation.
model_or_system: The model is quantum error correction, focusing on stabilizer codes and CSS codes defined over binary subspaces. The physical system involves encoding logical qubits into physical qubits to protect against errors while allowing selective gate operations.
key_observables: Code parameters include rate, distance ($d$), and the ability to realize specific logical gates (e.g., transversal T gate).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the code rate, the distance scaling ($\Omega(n)$ or $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$), and the gate order ($\ell$) for the implemented gates.
main_assumptions: The general case for arbitrary rational rotations requires the use of nonadditive codes, and the construction of Pauli-LDPC codes with fully addressable non-Clifford gates remains an open challenge.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing constructions for fully addressable transversal T gates in CSS codes, then detailing the use of algebraic geometry to enforce necessary phase identities, and finally presenting concrete constructions for sparse protected subsystems and distance lower bounds.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental limitations in fault-tolerant quantum computation by providing explicit constructions for high-performance quantum codes with necessary gate symmetries.
